text.p: Blue-chip stocks extended their winning streak Tuesday as a rally in bonds pushed the key long-term yield below the psychologically important 6.50 percent.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 7.83 points to 6,263.43, surpassing Monday's record close of 6,255.60, which was the index's fourth consecutive high.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on active volume of 264 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Tom Carpenter, chief economist for ASB Capital Management Inc., said bonds were one of the main reasons the Dow was able to maintain its advance into record territory.
"The fact that the Dow maintained the large advance yesterday and is now in record territory is a function of bonds," he said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 17/32, sending its yield down to 6.47 percent from 6.51 percent on Friday. The bond market was closed Monday for the Veterans' Day holiday.
The last time the bond yield dropped below 6.50 percent was on March 7, when it closed at 6.46 percent.
The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee meets Wednesday amid speculation that it will hold interest rates steady.

"We have that FOMC meeting, and although they are not expected to move on interest rates, there's some caution ahead of that, which can put a damper on things," said Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities.
Technology stocks failed to catch fire despite an espcially strong industry indicator, the October book-to-bill ratio, which beat even rosy expectations.

After Monday's market close, the Semiconductor Industry Association said the industry ratio of computer chip bookings to orders rose to 1.10 in October from 0.98 in September, stronger than analysts had expected.
"The book-to-bill ratio was a great number, but it really didn't do very much for technology stocks," Zagorski said.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 3.68 points at 1,266.35 after retreating from an early high of 1,268.60.
The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.16 at 580.89.

In special situations, Sunbeam stock was halted at 25-3/4. The appliance maker said it would cut 6,000 jobs, or half its work force, slash product lines and reduced its facilities to 14 from 53, and take a charge of $300 million.
Westinghouse jumped 1-1/8 to 21-1/8 on a report that it would spin off its industrial operations.
Microprocessor giant and industry flagship Intel Corp. was up 13/16 at 124-11/13, while PC graphics suppliers Chips and Technologies Inc. added 7/8 to 25-1/4.
